title: Regional warmup throttle and cache projections (Q4 2026)
summary: Quick model onboarding warmup plan for Q4 2026. This sheet projects per-region GPU demand and KV cache footprint across three rollout scenarios (staggered, burst, and adaptive warmup). Primary goal: quantify temporary headroom required and propose throttles/mitigations to keep latency SLOs while limiting capitalized burst capacity.
assumptions:
- New model family: rwx-13B and rwx-13B-quant-INT4 variant.
- Average request token length (LL): 120 tokens; 95th percentile 420 tokens.
- Cold KV cache miss rate for first 48 hours: 85% for rwx-13B, warms to 15% after 72h of steady traffic.
- Baseline per-region sustained throughput (existing served models): 80 GPU-hours/day per region reserved for rolling onboards.
- Warmup traffic pattern options: 'staggered' (2% daily ramp per region), 'burst' (20% of global traffic directed on day 1), 'adaptive' (prefill + controlled tail routing).
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU: 1200 for quant variant, 600 for fp16 profile (w/ current runtime kernels).
- KV footprint per active session avg: 1.2 MB/session for rwx-13B fp16, 0.5 MB/session for INT4 variant.
- Target latency SLO: p99 < 450ms for interactive routes (shorter contexts) and completion routes p95 < 1.2s.
- Available burst GPU capacity (soft): up to 30% of region fleet for 24h via preemptible pools.
projections:
Scenario: Staggered rollout (recommended default)
- Onboard cadence: 6 regions over 6 weeks, weekly region activation.
- Expected warmup QPS per region day0: 8% of steady-state traffic for first 24h, increasing to 35% by day7.
- GPU demand (per region):
  * Day0: additional 6 GPUs (INT4) or 12 GPUs (fp16) to hit p95 SLOs for short routes.
  * Peak (day3-day7): additional 18 GPUs (INT4) or 36 GPUs (fp16).
- KV cache footprint (per region):
  * Day0 sessions: 12k sessions -> KV = 12k * 0.5MB = 6.0 GB (INT4) or 12k * 1.2MB = 14.4 GB (fp16).
  * Peak day7 sessions: 58k sessions -> KV = 29 GB (INT4) or 69.6 GB (fp16).
- Storage IOPS / network egress stress: initial cache population causes ~1.2 GB/s sustained reads for 2h per region (prefetch pattern).

Scenario: Burst rollout (fast, riskier)
- Single global activation weekend sending 20% global traffic to new variants.
- GPU demand spike: equivalent of adding 120 INT4 GPUs global for 48h (or 240 fp16 GPUs).
- KV footprint global: 1.2M sessions cold -> 600 GB (INT4) / 1.44 TB (fp16).
- Risks: cross-region throttling, storage throttles, long-tailed p99 latency degradations, increased fallbacks to older model variants (cost & quality drift).

Scenario: Adaptive (preferred for constrained regions)
- Pre-warm KV for top 10k customer prefixes per region using traffic shadowing and persisted cache preloads.
- Controlled routing: route 10% of matched queries to new model, auto-scale up to safe CPU/GPU thresholds.
- Effective reduction in cold miss rate: from 85% -> ~28% for first 24h.
- Resulting GPU delta: 40% less than burst scenario and 20% less peak than naive staggered.
mitigation_plan:
1) Warmup policy: start with adaptive prefill for critical regions (us-west1, eu-west1) for top 20% customers. Use traffic shadowing and offline prefix replay to populate KV.
2) Soft-throttles: request-level token throttles (max tokens/sec per customer) and queue-based admission to keep tail latency within SLOs during first 72h.
3) KV eviction tuning: increase LRU window to 96h for warmed entries in region-local cache to reduce churn during rollout.
4) Progressive scaling: autoscaler profile 'onboard' that prioritizes INT4 instances; fallback to fp16 only when quality regression observed.
5) Rate-limiting fallback routes: automatic fallback to a pinned compatible variant (rwx-13B-lite) when p99 latency > 650ms for >5m.
6) Operational runbook snippets:
  - Alert: cache-populate-error > 5% for 30m -> reduce incoming new model qps by 50%.
  - Inspection step: check storage IOPS (CloudBlock metrics) and network egress.
7) Pre-bought burst pool: reserve 10% of target regional GPUs as preemptible burst and negotiate short-term capacity with cloud partner for weekend tops.
rollout_timeline:
Week 0: dry-run in staging with shadow traffic for top 5 prefixes (staging fleet).
Week 1: us-west1 adaptive prefill + 10% routed. Monitor warmup miss rate and p95 latency.
Week 2: eu-west1 adaptive prefill + 10% routed.
Week 3: ap-south1 staggered prefill (lower initial qps) + 5% routed.
Week 4: us-east1 progressive ramp to 25% if miss rate < 30% and p99 < 500ms.
Week 5: finalize region-specific cache tuning and expand to secondary regions.
Post-week 6: scale to full coverage if metrics stable for 72h per region.
notes:
- Quick checks for SRE on activation day: GPU utilization, queue depth, KV miss rate, storage read latency, network saturation per AZ.
- Cost estimate (staggered, 6-week): incremental burn ~ $145k (dominant cost: short-lived cloud GPUs and network). Burst scenario estimate: $1.1M over 72h.
- Follow-ups: build an automated 'prefill orchestrator' that accepts prefix lists, shards prefetch jobs across nodes, and tracks per-prefix warm metrics (INF-3857).
- Open questions: determine per-region KMS throughput limits when encrypting cached blobs; confirm cross-AZ egress pricing for staged prefill traffic.
